book.label: Venture book
book.mandate: Maximum gain in small caps, and nothing else. Candidates come from the top holdings of twenty small-cap ETFs, ranked by the signals with evidence behind them — earnings surprise, quality near a high, insider buying — with momentum and attention shown as context rather than used as the sort. Not funded; the risk policy of the other two books does not apply, and every number on the page is a base rate, not a forecast.

macro.summary: The Fed raised 25bp on 16 September to 3.75-4.00%, the first hike of the cycle, with futures pricing more before 2027. The Russell 2000 sits within 3% of its all-time high, up 29% from its 52-week low — but roughly 40% of the index is unprofitable and carries floating-rate debt, and each 25bp costs the index about 2% of operating earnings. The environment punishes exactly the names a naive breakout screen surfaces and favours the profitable, cash-generative ones the panel evidence favours too.
points: Fed +25bp on 2026-09-16 to 3.75-4.00%; CME priced a two-in-three chance beforehand.
Russell 2000 at ~2,972, within 3% of its high; small caps still at a discount to large.
~40% of the Russell 2000 unprofitable and floating-rate levered; BofA: each 25bp ≈ -2% index operating earnings.
Small-cap interest expense reprices with the Fed almost in real time.
Emerging industries in the backdrop: AI data-centre power and electrification, SMR nuclear, defence and counter-drone, space (SpaceX IPO catalyst), quantum, optical connectivity.

evidence.label: Earnings surprise
evidence.note: Top quintile of standardised surprise among the screened names (threshold printed on the run), SUE at least 1. Post-earnings drift is declining in large caps and strongest in small, thinly covered ones; in this panel top-decile SUE runs +3.8pp/yr over the universe (t = 1.4).

evidence.label: Quality near its high
evidence.note: GP/A (Novy-Marx) of 0.25 or more and price within 10% of its 52-week high; financials excluded, as in the literature. The one profile that reaches t = 2.1 in this panel (3-month horizon); +5.3pp/yr at 12 months, t = 1.3.

evidence.label: Insider cluster buying
evidence.note: Two or more insiders buying with their own cash inside 45 days. Small-cap insider purchases earned ~7.4% abnormal over twelve months; opportunistic buys ~4x routine ones. Not in the panel.

evidence.label: Insider purchase
evidence.note: At least one open-market purchase in 90 days. Awards, exercises and gifts do not count.

evidence.label: A tracked fund's best idea
evidence.note: Top-ten position by value in the latest 13F of a concentrated or activist manager. Requires SEC_CONTACT to fetch; absent otherwise.

evidence.label: Held by 2+ tracked funds
evidence.note: Present in the latest 13F of two or more tracked managers, at any weight.

evidence.label: Analyst initiation
evidence.note: Coverage initiated in the last 90 days: ~0.8% abnormal over the initiation week. An event, not a screen.

evidence.label: Near high on low volatility
evidence.note: Within 5% of the 52-week high with below-median volatility and no volume surge. Doubles most often of the near-high profiles in the panel (7.6%); t = 0.4.

evidence.label: Near 52-week high
evidence.note: Within 5% of the 52-week high. Shown, not scored: the 52-week-high effect is explained by price momentum, which is negative in this universe.

evidence.label: Breakout + momentum + volume
evidence.note: The classic pre-run profile. In this panel it underperforms the universe by 3.4pp/yr and doubles least often of any bucket. Shown because it was asked for; not rewarded.

evidence.label: Reports within 3 weeks
evidence.note: A catalyst date, not a direction.

evidence.label: Attention spike
evidence.note: News-mention spike of 2 sigma or more against the name's own baseline. Retail attention predicts reversal: -8.5% HPR at peak WSB attention; 3-sigma spikes -0.52% over five days.

evidence.label: Unprofitable and levered
evidence.note: Negative TTM net income with net debt, or net debt over 3x EBITDA. The slice of the Russell 2000 each 25bp hike hurts most (BofA: ~-2% index operating earnings per hike).

evidence.label: Net downgrades
evidence.note: More downgrades than upgrades in 90 days.

evidence.label: Down 30%+ in six months
evidence.note: Bottom-decile momentum names double most often in the panel (10.8%) and halve most often (25.4%). Lottery odds, shown as such.
